newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar stays weak, expiry trades prevail.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar stays weak, expiry trades prevail.

text.p: White sugar futures stayed weak during Monday afternoon trading as players started to square their books with the approach of the spot May expiry, traders said.
One leading commission house set the pace of the day's activity and dominated the overall turnover with crossed May/August and against actuals trades on May.
Other commission house sellers caused the May/August to narrow slightly to around $2.00.
Traders said next week's May expiry on April 15 was starting to attract increased nearby spread trades as spot positions were rolled forward.
"We're starting to see some of that," said one.
At 1540 GMT May stood $1.10 lower at $309.80 and August down 40 cents at $307.70. Trades in the two front months, principally May, accounted for the bulk of the solid overall volume of 2,361 lots.
Traders said there was little arbitrage activity against the New York raws market with May/May valued at around $67, slightly narrower than on Friday.
Paris positions were also slightly weaker with volume mostly coming from trades in the spot May position, which expires on the same day as its London equivalent.
May was down 60 cents at $310.20 and August down 30 cents at $307.80. Matif volume totalled 550 lots.
